summary: A private contemporary-art museum in a converted industrial building east of Chiang Mai. Shortlist it for Thai and regional art, installation and moving-image work, and the memorable mirrored exterior. It is a purposeful excursion rather than an Old City walk-in; whether it earns the drive depends on your interest in the exhibitions running during your stay.
whyGo: See contemporary Thailand through artists rather than temples and heritage displays.
Enjoy architecture, art books and museum-shop browsing in one compact visit.
bestFor: Travellers wanting a quieter indoor cultural stop
skipIf: Abstract or conceptual art rarely interests you
You have very limited Chiang Mai time and prefer walkable sights
duration: Allow 1.5–2 hours for galleries, longer for films or the café; this is a planning estimate, plus travel.
cost: Official visit page lists adults THB 200, students THB 100 and seniors THB 150. Add transport and any food; concession eligibility and December pricing need reconfirmation.
hours: 10:00–18:00, but official pages conflict: the homepage and footer say Friday–Monday, while the visit-page body says every day except Tuesday. Choose Friday–Monday provisionally and confirm before travelling.
bestTime: Start near opening, with plenty of time for slow viewing and arranging the return journey.
gettingThere: 122 Moo 7, Tonpao, San Kamphaeng, on old San Kamphaeng Road/1006. The museum estimates 20 minutes from central Chiang Mai; allow extra traffic time. Grab or a hired driver is the simplest planning option; check the fare in-app. Parking is listed. Official white-minibus information appears dated and is not a dependable timetable.
booking: No mandatory general-entry reservation was established. Check the official exhibition and event listings before visiting; workshops and special events may have separate arrangements.
accessibility: Step-free routes, accessible toilets, seating and sensory provisions were not verified; visitors requiring these should confirm directly before committing to the trip.
practicalTips: Arrange your return transport before a late-afternoon visit.
Check photography rules for individual artworks; exterior photographs do not establish gallery permissions.
The official site lists a café and shop, but their separate operating hours were not confirmed.
decemberNotes: December 2026 exhibition details remain uncertain. The official listing says October 6th: a reconfigured archive ends 30 November 2026, so do not shortlist on that exhibition alone. Other homepage dates are displayed ambiguously. Recheck the actual December programme and holiday opening days shortly before departure.
uncertainties: Current public-minibus service, fare and return frequency
